slots.practicalActivity: Sign in to the Fabric portal at app.fabric.microsoft.com with a trial capacity, create a new workspace named nyc_taxi_fabric, and tour its item types (Lakehouse, Warehouse, Notebook, Pipeline, Eventstream) to see where each one of this course's chapters will live.
slots.deliverable: A live Fabric workspace named nyc_taxi_fabric, with a short note listing the item types you found available to create inside it.

lessons.title: OneLake — One Lake for the Whole Organization

slots.practicalActivity: Open the OneLake file explorer (or the OneLake tab in Fabric) and locate your workspace's storage path, then create a new Lakehouse named nyc_taxi_lakehouse and upload a sample NYC Taxi CSV into its Files area before loading it into a new Delta table under Tables.
slots.deliverable: A nyc_taxi_lakehouse with the raw CSV sitting in Files and a trips Delta table created from it under Tables, confirmed queryable from the Lakehouse's SQL endpoint.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Fabric notebook, attach it to nyc_taxi_lakehouse, and run a PySpark cell that reads the trips Delta table and prints its row count and schema, then write a short comparison note on what felt identical to Azure Databricks notebooks and what felt different (default Spark session, attached Lakehouse context, UI layout).
slots.deliverable: A Fabric notebook that successfully reads trips and prints its schema/row count, plus a written comparison of Fabric notebooks vs. Databricks notebooks from the earlier course.

lessons.title: Shortcuts — Referencing Data Without Copying It

slots.practicalActivity: Create a OneLake Shortcut inside nyc_taxi_lakehouse pointing at another location (an ADLS Gen2 container or a second lakehouse) and confirm the data is queryable without being copied, then build a simple Data Factory pipeline in Fabric with a Copy activity that moves a file into the lakehouse's Files area.
slots.deliverable: A working Shortcut whose referenced data is queryable from the lakehouse without duplication, plus a Data Factory pipeline that ran a Copy activity successfully at least once.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Dataflow Gen2 that uses the Power Query editor to clean a column (e.g., trim/rename a field) in the taxi CSV and load the result into the lakehouse, then create a Fabric Warehouse and load a summary table into it with a plain T-SQL CREATE TABLE and INSERT statement.
slots.deliverable: A Dataflow Gen2 whose output table lands in the lakehouse, plus a Fabric Warehouse containing one table created and populated with real T-SQL.

lessons.title: Lakehouse vs. Warehouse — Choosing the Right Engine

slots.practicalActivity: Run the same aggregate query against both the lakehouse's SQL endpoint and the Fabric Warehouse to compare the experience, then build a Power BI report in Direct Lake mode directly against the trips Delta table and confirm a visual renders without a separate import/refresh step.
slots.deliverable: A short written comparison of querying the lakehouse SQL endpoint vs. the Warehouse, plus a Power BI report with at least one visual built in Direct Lake mode against trips.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the default semantic model created alongside nyc_taxi_lakehouse, add one measure (e.g., a DAX SUM of fare_amount), then check the workspace's assigned capacity and SKU under Workspace settings and note its capacity units.
slots.deliverable: The lakehouse's default semantic model with one new working DAX measure added, plus a recorded note of the workspace's capacity SKU and capacity units.

lessons.title: Fabric Chapter Recap — Where This Fits With Databricks

slots.practicalActivity: Connect the nyc_taxi_fabric workspace to a Git repository (Azure DevOps or GitHub) and commit its current items, create a Deployment Pipeline with Dev/Test/Prod stages and deploy the workspace content into a Test stage, then check the Monitoring Hub for the recent notebook, pipeline, and Dataflow runs from this chapter.
slots.deliverable: A Git-connected workspace with at least one commit, a Deployment Pipeline that has deployed content into a Test stage, and a Monitoring Hub screenshot-free summary listing this chapter's recent item runs.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review lab for Microsoft Fabric: without new instruction, build one small end-to-end artifact combining a lakehouse, a Data Factory pipeline that loads a new file into it, a Dataflow Gen2 transformation, and a Direct Lake Power BI report — then write a short mapping of each Fabric piece to its Azure Databricks & Delta Lake equivalent from the prior course.
slots.deliverable: One original mini-pipeline (lakehouse + Data Factory pipeline + Dataflow Gen2 + Direct Lake report) built without re-watching lessons, plus a written Fabric-to-Databricks concept mapping table.

slots.practicalActivity: Review the Real-Time Intelligence item types available in the workspace, then create a new Eventstream item named nyc_taxi_eventstream and open its editor to see the source/transformation/destination canvas before wiring anything to it.
slots.deliverable: A created Eventstream item (nyc_taxi_eventstream) with its empty source/transformation/destination canvas open, plus a one-sentence note on what Real-Time Intelligence covers that batch lakehouse pipelines don't.

lessons.title: Event Sources: Azure Event Hubs and IoT Hub

slots.practicalActivity: Connect an Azure Event Hub (or the Eventstream's built-in sample data source if no Event Hub is available) as the source for nyc_taxi_eventstream, then create an Eventhouse with a KQL database inside it and wire it as the Eventstream's destination.
slots.deliverable: An Eventstream with a configured source and an Eventhouse/KQL database configured as its destination, both visible and connected in the Eventstream canvas.

lessons.title: KQL: Basic Queries With where and project

slots.practicalActivity: Open a KQL Queryset against the new KQL database and write a query chaining where to filter rows with fare_amount > 0, then project to select and rename a handful of columns, confirming the pipe-chain syntax runs end to end.
slots.deliverable: A saved KQL query in the Queryset combining where and project against the live table, returning a filtered, renamed-column result set.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a KQL summarize query computing count() and avg(fare_amount) grouped by VendorID, then ingest a small second reference table (e.g., a vendor lookup) into the KQL database and write a join query combining it with the trip events table.
slots.deliverable: A working summarize aggregation query and a working join query against two tables in the KQL database, both saved in the Queryset.

lessons.title: Ingesting Data Into a KQL Database

slots.practicalActivity: Write a make-series query bucketing trip counts into one-minute bins over the last 30 minutes of ingested data, then configure continuous ingestion from the Eventstream into the KQL database's RawTripEvents table if not already streaming, confirming new rows keep landing without manual re-runs.
slots.deliverable: A make-series time-bucketed query returning results, plus confirmed continuous ingestion into RawTripEvents shown by two row-count checks a few minutes apart that differ.

slots.practicalActivity: Real-time ingestion lab: stand up the complete source-to-query chain from scratch — an Event Hub (or sample) source feeding nyc_taxi_eventstream, landing in an Eventhouse/KQL database table, queried with a where/project/summarize chain you write without re-watching lessons — using simulated NYC Taxi trip events end to end.
slots.deliverable: One independently rebuilt source -> Eventstream -> Eventhouse/KQL chain with a working KQL query proving rows are landing and queryable, built from a blank workspace item set.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Real-Time Dashboard and add one tile built from a KQL query (e.g., trip count over the last 15 minutes rendered as a timechart), setting the dashboard to auto-refresh, then review the windowing concepts you'll apply in the next slots against your own streaming trip data.
slots.deliverable: A Real-Time Dashboard with at least one auto-refreshing tile backed by a live KQL query against RawTripEvents.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a KQL query using bin() to compute non-overlapping tumbling-window trip counts (one-minute buckets), then write a second query simulating a hopping/sliding window (e.g., a 5-minute window advancing every 1 minute) and compare how the two outputs differ for the same underlying stream.
slots.deliverable: Two saved KQL queries — one tumbling-window and one hopping/sliding-window aggregation over the same trip stream — with a short note on how their results differ for overlapping time ranges.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a session-window-style KQL query grouping events by VendorID into sessions separated by a gap of inactivity, then configure a watermark/late-arrival setting on the Eventstream (or document the equivalent KQL ingestion-time policy) and test it by sending one deliberately late-timestamped event.
slots.deliverable: A working session-window query, plus a documented watermark/late-arrival configuration proven by one deliberately late event being handled according to the configured policy rather than silently misprocessed.

slots.practicalActivity: Send a small batch of deliberately out-of-order events into the Eventstream and confirm they're still processed correctly downstream, then add a Filter and a Manage Fields transformation to the Eventstream canvas, and configure it to route output to two destinations at once (the KQL database and the lakehouse).
slots.deliverable: Confirmed correct handling of an out-of-order test batch, plus an Eventstream with a Filter transformation, a Manage Fields transformation, and two active destinations (KQL database and lakehouse) both receiving data.

slots.practicalActivity: Create an Activator rule watching the trip stream for FareAmount > 200 and configure it to send a Teams or email notification, triggering it once with a deliberately high test fare, then review/configure a CDC-streamed source (or document the pattern against a SQL table with change tracking enabled) feeding into the Eventstream.
slots.deliverable: A confirmed Activator alert fired by one deliberate high-fare test event, plus a documented or configured CDC-streamed source pattern feeding the Eventstream.

lessons.title: Comparing Fabric Real-Time to Databricks Structured Streaming

slots.practicalActivity: Add a data-quality filter transformation to the Eventstream that drops events with a null or negative fare_amount before they reach the KQL database, then write a comparison note on Fabric's Eventstream/Activator model versus the Structured Streaming + watermarking approach from the Azure Databricks & Delta Lake course.
slots.deliverable: An Eventstream with an active quality filter proven by sending one deliberately bad event and confirming it never reaches the KQL database, plus a written Fabric-vs-Databricks streaming comparison note.

slots.practicalActivity: Windowing and alerting lab: without new instruction, extend your Eventstream with one tumbling or sliding window query feeding a dashboard tile, plus a second Activator rule of your own design (different condition than the fare-amount example), and a data-quality filter — then trigger each piece once to confirm it fires correctly.
slots.deliverable: One extended Eventstream pipeline with an original window query, an original Activator rule, and a quality filter, each independently triggered and confirmed working.

lessons.title: A Real-Time NYC Taxi Dashboard, Start to Finish

slots.practicalActivity: Assemble the full pipeline this lesson walks through end to end against your own workspace: source -> Eventstream (filter + window) -> KQL database -> Real-Time Dashboard tile -> Activator rule, confirming every stage is wired and live, then write a short chapter recap listing every real-time concept you've now built hands-on.
slots.deliverable: One confirmed end-to-end real-time pipeline (source through dashboard and alert) running in your workspace, plus a written recap listing every real-time concept applied.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter capstone review for Real-Time Data Engineering: extend the real-time NYC Taxi dashboard with one original enhancement not covered step-by-step in any lesson — for example a second dashboard tile using a different window type, or a new Activator rule on a different condition — and demonstrate the full chain still working together.
slots.deliverable: The real-time dashboard pipeline extended with one original enhancement, demonstrated working end to end from source event through the new dashboard tile or alert.

slots.practicalActivity: Score the nyc_taxi_fabric workspace's existing pipeline against a production-readiness checklist (testing, monitoring, alerting, documentation, access control), then set up separate Dev/Test/Prod workspaces using Fabric Deployment Pipeline stages for this course's lakehouse and pipeline items.
slots.deliverable: A written production-readiness scorecard for your current pipeline, plus a Deployment Pipeline with Dev/Test/Prod stages configured for the workspace's lakehouse and pipeline items.

lessons.title: Version Control for Notebooks and Pipelines

slots.practicalActivity: Set up a CI/CD workflow (Azure DevOps Pipelines or GitHub Actions) that promotes the Git-connected workspace's items from Dev to Test automatically on a commit, confirming the Git integration from Chapter 1 is doing real version control for the notebooks and pipeline definitions involved.
slots.deliverable: A working CI/CD workflow definition (YAML) that triggers a Deployment Pipeline promotion on commit, with at least one successful run confirmed in the CI/CD tool's run history.

lessons.title: Infrastructure as Code — ARM/Bicep and Terraform Basics

slots.practicalActivity: Write a small Bicep or Terraform file that provisions a Fabric capacity (or an equivalent Azure resource used by this course, such as the Event Hub namespace), then deploy it with `az deployment group create` (Bicep) or `terraform apply` and confirm the resource appears in the Azure portal.
slots.deliverable: One Bicep or Terraform file successfully deployed, with the provisioned resource confirmed visible in the Azure portal and the IaC file saved for reuse.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a pytest unit test for one PySpark transformation function used in this course's pipeline (e.g., the fare-cleaning or windowing logic), running it locally or in a Fabric notebook cell against a small hand-built sample DataFrame to assert the output matches expectations.
slots.deliverable: At least one passing pytest unit test for a real PySpark transformation function from this course, including one deliberately broken input case the test correctly catches.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a simple data contract document (expected schema, types, and value constraints) for the trips table, then deliberately introduce a breaking schema change upstream (rename or drop a column the contract expects) and observe how the downstream pipeline step fails or misbehaves.
slots.deliverable: A written data contract for the trips table, plus a documented breaking-change test showing exactly what failed downstream when the contract was violated.

slots.practicalActivity: Testing and contracts lab: combine this section's pieces into one validated build — the pytest unit test from the previous slot, the data contract for trips, and a deliberate schema-drift scenario — into a single notebook or pipeline run that catches the bad change before it reaches the gold layer.
slots.deliverable: One pipeline run where a deliberately introduced schema-drift change is caught before reaching gold output, backed by the pytest unit test and the documented data contract.

lessons.title: Setting Up Alerts for Pipeline Failures

slots.practicalActivity: Add logging statements (row counts, timings) to one of this course's pipeline notebooks and review them in the Monitoring Hub's run details, then configure a Fabric Data Factory pipeline failure alert (email or Teams) and test it by deliberately pointing a Copy activity at a bad source path.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline run with visible custom log output in the Monitoring Hub, plus a confirmed failure alert triggered by one deliberately broken pipeline run.

slots.practicalActivity: Review the workspace's capacity metrics app (or billing/cost report) for compute usage over the past runs, then adjust the Spark pool/session size (or capacity SKU) used by one of this course's notebooks and re-run it, comparing execution time and reported usage before and after the change.
slots.deliverable: A before/after comparison of execution time and reported capacity usage for one notebook run under two different compute sizing settings.

lessons.title: SLAs and SLOs for Data Pipelines

slots.practicalActivity: Write a concrete SLO for this course's daily gold refresh pipeline (e.g., "95% of days, gold_daily_revenue is refreshed by 7:00 AM") and design a real way to measure it using the Monitoring Hub's run timestamps, then check the last several actual run times against that target.
slots.deliverable: A written SLO for the pipeline plus an actual measurement against several real run timestamps from the Monitoring Hub, stating whether the SLO was met.

lessons.title: Root Cause Analysis, Step by Step

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately break one pipeline step (e.g., point a Copy activity at a renamed/missing file), run an incident-response drill by following a simple triage checklist to locate the failure in the Monitoring Hub, then perform a root-cause analysis write-up explaining exactly why it failed and the fix applied.
slots.deliverable: A documented incident-response drill log and a root-cause analysis write-up for one deliberately broken pipeline run, ending with the fix applied and the pipeline confirmed working again.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a disaster-recovery plan for nyc_taxi_lakehouse (what gets backed up, how it would be restored, acceptable data loss window), then document a data-governance policy for the workspace covering who owns which tables and how changes get reviewed.
slots.deliverable: A written disaster-recovery plan and a written data-governance policy document, both specific to the actual lakehouse and pipelines built in this course.

slots.practicalActivity: Identify a column in the trips data that would be sensitive in a real system (e.g., a driver ID or payment card last-4) and apply a masking or hashing transformation to it before it reaches gold, then move one hardcoded connection string or key used anywhere in this course's pipelines into Azure Key Vault (or Fabric's connection credentials) instead of leaving it in plain text.
slots.deliverable: A masked/hashed sensitive column in the gold output, plus at least one connection secret migrated out of plain text into Key Vault or a managed Fabric connection, confirmed still working.

slots.practicalActivity: Review every workspace role assignment and item-level permission in nyc_taxi_fabric, removing or downgrading at least one over-broad grant to match least privilege, then write a capacity-planning estimate for what SKU/capacity this pipeline would need if the source data volume grew 10x.
slots.deliverable: A documented access review with at least one permission tightened, plus a written capacity-planning estimate justifying a specific SKU for 10x the current data volume.

slots.practicalActivity: Governance and reliability lab: combine this section's pieces into one hardened, documented workspace configuration — the PII masking from an earlier slot, the migrated secret, the tightened access review, and the disaster-recovery plan — written up as a single governance document for the nyc_taxi_fabric workspace.
slots.deliverable: One consolidated governance document covering PII handling, secrets management, access control, and disaster recovery for the actual workspace built in this course.

lessons.title: Blue-Green and Canary Deployments for Pipelines

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy a changed version of one pipeline to the Test stage alongside the existing Prod version (a simple blue-green setup using two Deployment Pipeline stages) and run both briefly, then deliberately roll the Prod stage back to the previous Deployment Pipeline version and confirm the rollback restored the earlier behavior.
slots.deliverable: A documented blue-green deployment test comparing two pipeline versions, plus a confirmed rollback of the Prod stage back to its prior Deployment Pipeline snapshot.

slots.practicalActivity: Write real documentation for this course's end-to-end pipeline that a new on-call engineer could use cold (what it does, how to check if it's healthy, where the logs are), then draft an on-call runbook entry for the single most likely failure mode you've actually seen while building this course.
slots.deliverable: A written pipeline README and a one-page on-call runbook entry for the most likely real failure mode, both specific to this course's actual nyc_taxi_fabric pipeline.

lessons.title: A Production Incident, Start to Finish

slots.practicalActivity: Run the full incident drill end to end exactly as this capstone lesson walks through: break the pipeline deliberately, get paged by the alert from an earlier slot, follow your own runbook entry to triage and find the root cause in the Monitoring Hub, fix it, and roll it back out through the Deployment Pipeline.
slots.deliverable: A complete written incident timeline — alert fired, runbook followed, root cause found, fix applied, redeployed through the Deployment Pipeline — for one real deliberately-triggered failure.

lessons.title: Production Data Engineering Recap — and This Course's Finale

slots.practicalActivity: Walk back through every workspace item built across all three chapters of this course (lakehouse, warehouse, Dataflow, Eventstream, Eventhouse/KQL database, dashboard, Activator rules, Deployment Pipeline stages, IaC files, CI/CD workflow) and list them in one complete inventory.
slots.deliverable: A complete written inventory of every Fabric item and supporting artifact (IaC file, CI/CD workflow, runbook, governance doc) built across the entire course.

slots.practicalActivity: Course and chapter final review: produce one polished portfolio write-up documenting the complete production-hardening journey applied to this course's NYC Taxi pipeline — CI/CD and IaC, testing and data contracts, observability and alerting, cost/right-sizing, governance and PII handling, and the full incident-response drill — ready to present in a job interview.
slots.deliverable: One polished portfolio document covering CI/CD, testing, observability, cost management, governance, and incident response as actually applied to this course's real NYC Taxi pipeline, suitable for sharing with an interviewer.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After completing this course, a student can build and govern Microsoft Fabric lakehouses, warehouses, and pipelines; design and operate a real-time Eventstream-to-Eventhouse-to-KQL-dashboard pipeline with windowing and Activator alerting; and apply production data engineering practices — CI/CD, infrastructure as code, testing, observability, cost management, governance, and incident response — to a real running pipeline.
